Let $y=2^{x}>0$. Then $2^{2x+1}=2\cdot(2^{x})^{2}=2y^{2}$ and $2^{x+1}=2y$. The equation becomes $2y^{2}+2y-80=0$, i.e. $y^{2}+y-40=0$. Hence $y=\frac{-1+\sqrt{161}}{2}$ (the positive root). Therefore $2^{x}=\frac{-1+\sqrt{161}}{2}$, so $x=\log_{2}\bigl(\tfrac{-1+\sqrt{161}}{2}\bigr)$.
